El entrelazamiento cuántico es un fenómeno que se produce cuando se genera un grupo de partículas, interactúan entre ellas o comparten proximidad espacial de tal manera que el estado cuántico de cada partícula del grupo no puede describirse independientemente del estado de las demás, incluso cuando las partículas están separadas por una gran distancia. El tema del entrelazamiento cuántico se sitúa en el centro de la disparidad existente entre la física clásica y la cuántica: el entrelazamiento es una característica primordial de la mecánica cuántica que no está presente en la mecánica clásica.

Las dimensiones de las propiedades físicas como la posición, el momento, el espín y la polarización realizadas en partículas entrelazadas pueden, en algunos casos, estar perfectamente correlacionadas. Por ejemplo, si se generan un par de partículas entrelazadas de forma que se sabe que su espín total es cero, y se descubre que una partícula tiene un espín en el sentido de las agujas del reloj en un primer eje, entonces se descubre que el espín de la otra partícula, medido en el mismo eje, será contrario a las agujas del reloj. Sin embargo, este comportamiento da lugar a efectos aparentemente paradójicos: cualquier medición de las propiedades de una partícula provoca un colapso aparente e irreversible de la función de onda de esta partícula y cambia el estado cuántico original. Con partículas entrelazadas, estas mediciones afectan al sistema de entrelazado en su conjunto.

Estos fenómenos fueron el tema principal del artículo publicado en 1935 por Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky y Nathan Rosen, y de varios artículos escritos poco después por Erwin Schrödinger, donde se describía lo que se conoce como la paradoja EPR. Einstein y compañía consideraron que este comportamiento era imposible, ya que incumplía el punto de vista del realismo local de la causalidad (Einstein se refirió a él como "una acción espeluznante a distancia") y argumentaron que la formulación aceptada de la mecánica cuántica debía ser, por tanto, incompleta.

The phenomenon of quantum entanglement occurs when a group of particles interact or share proximity in such a way that the quantum state of each particle in the group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, even when the particles are separated by a great distance. The topic of quantum entanglement sits at the heart of the disparity between classical and quantum physics: entanglement is a fundamental characteristic of quantum mechanics that is not present in classical mechanics.
The dimensions of physical properties such as position, momentum, spin and polarization made in entangled particles can, in some cases, be perfectly correlated. For example, if a pair of entangled particles are created so that it is known that their total spin is zero, and one particle is found to have a spin in the clockwise direction on one axis, then the spin of the other particle, measured on the same axis, will be found to be counterclockwise. However, this behavior gives rise to apparently paradoxical effects: any measurement of a property of one particle collapses the wave function of the entire entangled system, affecting the entangled system as a whole.
These phenomena were the subject of the 1935 paper by Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky and Nathan Rosen, and of several papers written shortly afterwards by Erwin Schrödinger, describing what has become known as the EPR paradox. Einstein and colleagues considered this behavior to be impossible, as it violated the principle of local realism of causality (Einstein referred to it as "spooky action at a distance") and argued that the accepted formulation of quantum mechanics must therefore be incomplete.

Assessing the Importance of Conservation in Protecting the Environment
The world has always been an amazing place to live in, with a plethora of natural resources that are essential to our survival. However, in recent years, the environment has been under increasing strain, with human activities such as deforestation, pollution, and climate change threatening the delicate balance of the planet. It is, therefore, essential to recognize the importance of conservation in protecting the environment and preserving the natural resources that we rely on.
One of the main reasons why conservation is essential is that it helps to protect biodiversity. Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth, and it is essential for the functioning of ecosystems. Without biodiversity, ecosystems would be unable to sustain themselves, and species would become extinct. Conservation helps to protect endangered species and their habitats, ensuring that future generations can enjoy the beauty and diversity of nature.
Another critical reason why conservation is essential is that it helps to protect the environment from human activities. Human activities such as deforestation, pollution, and climate change can have devastating effects on the environment. Conservation helps to mitigate the impact of these activities by promoting sustainable practices, such as renewable energy sources and organic farming.
Furthermore, conservation helps to promote economic growth and development. Conservation can create jobs in the tourism and conservation sectors, which can help to boost the local economy. Additionally, conservation can attract investment in sustainable industries, such as renewable energy and organic farming, which can help to create new jobs and businesses.
Finally, conservation is essential because it helps to promote a sense of stewardship for the environment. By conserving the environment, we are taking responsibility for the planet and ensuring that future generations can enjoy its beauty and resources. Conservation can also help to promote a sense of community and shared responsibility for the environment, which can help to build a stronger and more sustainable society.
In conclusion, conservation is essential for protecting the environment and preserving the natural resources that we rely on. It helps to protect biodiversity, mitigate the impact of human activities, promote economic growth and development, and promote a sense of stewardship for the environment. As such, it is crucial that we all do our part to support conservation efforts and help to ensure a sustainable future for the planet.
